description: SE322 final roadmap: how quality attributes, architecture, detailed design, design patterns, evaluation and documentation fit together, with the material to study for every topic, look-alike concepts side by side, and a coverage tracker.
lede: Every SE322 topic answers one question at one zoom level. Work top to bottom: what the system must achieve, its big parts, the classes inside a part, the proven class designs, then checking and recording it all. When two things look alike, first ask which level each one lives on.

confusables.title: Architectural style vs architectural pattern vs design pattern
confusables.ask: How much of the system does it shape?
rows: The overall template for a family of systems
A reusable solution for the whole system's structure
A class-level solution inside one subsystem
test: You choose Observer so the views refresh when the model changes. Which level are you working at?
Design pattern: it organizes classes inside the system. MVC, the architecture, happens to use it.

confusables.title: Architecture vs detailed design
confusables.ask: Are you looking at the box from outside or opening it?
rows: Black box: major components and connectors, mostly quality requirements
White box: classes, algorithms and interfaces inside one component
test: Deciding that the payment service talks to the order service through a broker: architecture or detailed design?
Architecture: it is about components and how they connect.

confusables.title: Factory Method vs Abstract Factory vs Builder
confusables.ask: One product, a matching family, or one complex object built in steps?
rows: One product type; a subclass decides the concrete class
Several related products that must match
One complex object assembled in the same steps
test: A UI kit must create buttons, menus and dialogs that all match the chosen theme. Which pattern?
Abstract Factory: a family of products that must match.

confusables.title: Singleton vs Prototype
confusables.ask: Exactly one object, or copies of one?
rows: Exactly one instance with global access
New objects made by cloning an existing one
test: Creating many similar enemies is expensive, so you copy a configured one. Which pattern?
Prototype.

confusables.title: Adapter vs Facade vs Composite
confusables.ask: Converting one interface, simplifying many, or treating a tree uniformly?
rows: Wraps one class so it fits the interface a client expects
One simple entry point in front of a subsystem
ShopKeeper in front of the phone classes
Parts and wholes share one interface
Folder and File both have getSize()
test: An old library has pay(amountCents) but your code calls charge(Money). Which pattern?
Adapter.

confusables.title: Observer vs MVC
rows: Design pattern: a subject notifies registered observers
test: Inside MVC, how does the model tell the views it changed?
Through Observer: the model is the subject, the views are observers.

confusables.title: Client-server vs broker vs peer-to-peer
confusables.ask: Who knows where the server is, and is there a centre at all?
rows: Clients call a known central server (tightly coupled)
A broker locates servers; clients never need their address
Every node is both client and server
test: Clients request services without knowing which machine provides them. Which pattern?
Broker.

confusables.title: Pipes-and-filters vs layered vs blackboard
confusables.ask: Data in a line, levels serving the level above, or experts sharing one store?
rows: Independent stages; output of one is input of the next
Each layer uses only the layer below
Agents read and write a shared store in no fixed order
test: Separate experts for sound, words and grammar each add partial results to shared data. Which pattern?
Blackboard.

confusables.title: Abstraction vs encapsulation vs separating interface and implementation
confusables.ask: Choosing what matters, hiding it, or allowing many implementations behind one face?
rows: Enforces the abstraction by hiding internals
Several implementations behind one stable interface
test: Callers only see a Repository interface, so you can swap the database engine. Which principle?
Separation of interface and implementation.

confusables.title: SOLID look-alikes
confusables.ask: A class doing too much, a fat interface, code you must edit, a broken subtype, or a concrete dependency?
rows: More than one reason to change
Clients forced to depend on unused methods
Adding a case means editing working code
A subtype breaks the base contract
High-level code depends on a concrete class
test: FundTransferManager calls BankAccount directly. Which principle, and the fix?
Dependency Inversion: introduce ITransferSource and ITransferDestination.

confusables.title: Functional requirement vs quality attribute vs tactic
confusables.ask: What it does, how well, or the design decision that achieves it?
rows: How well, judged on the whole system
A design decision that controls an attribute's response
test: "Use a cache to keep responses under 2 seconds." Which part is the tactic?
The cache is the tactic; "under 2 seconds" is the performance attribute's measure.

confusables.title: Risk vs sensitivity point vs trade-off point
confusables.ask: Threatens a goal, strongly moves one attribute, or pulls several in opposite directions?
rows: A decision that may cause problems for a quality goal
Affects several attributes in opposite directions
test: More replicas improve availability but slow down keeping data consistent. What is it in ATAM?
A trade-off point.
